articles.title: Harry Kane: Striker's rise from childhood keeper to England great
articles.summary: Harry Kane reaches another significant England milestone by equalling Peter Shilton's record as the most-capped Three Lions player that he has held for 36 years.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has reached another significant England milestone by equalling Peter Shilton's 36-year-old record as the most-capped Three Lions player.

The Bayern Munich striker made his 125th appearance for the national team against the Czech Republic in the Nations League on Tuesday.

Kane is already his country's record scorer with 89 goals in 124 appearances in a full international career he started by opening his account 79 seconds into his debut.

Goalkeeper Shilton congratulated Kane for equalling his record, writing on social media: "You will go on and beat it in November I am sure of that, and maybe go on and set a record that may never be beaten.

"You're still going strong Harry, still playing well and scoring goals. I know how much dedication and hard work you put into achieving this, especially as a striker as I think that is probably the hardest position to play with goalkeeper just behind it.

"You've been a great captain and will be in the future."

BBC Sport takes a look at the origins story of the England captain.

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

When a six-year-old Harry Kane arrived for trials with Ridgeway Rovers in 1999, the youth side - who a generation earlier had produced David Beckham - thought they had found themselves a new goalkeeper.

Dave Bricknell, former Ridgeway Rovers coach: "We're doing a little shooting session, and I ask for a lad who can go in goal.

"This little boy puts his hand up and says: 'I'll go in goal.' We give him some gloves, and he performs heroics - makes some fantastic saves. He's tipping it round the post, tipping a couple over the bar.

"I'm thinking this is great, we've got a goalkeeper. And then this woman came up to me and said he's better on the pitch.

"We put him on pitch and he smacked goals in left, right and centre. So he ends up being our centre-forward."

Kane's prolific form for Ridgeway Rovers and his Waltham Forest district side caught the attention of professional scouts. Arsenal initially snapped up the youngster but decided not to keep him, while Watford also passed up the opportunity to sign Kane.

Trevor Bailey, Kane's manager at Waltham Forest: "Harry could have done nothing all game, but if that chance came up it was in the onion bag.

"He was always on the move up front. When he got a chance, guaranteed four out of five he was going to score or set someone up."

Alex Welsh, former academy coach at Arsenal: "I first met Harry in the academy and he was a very competent goalkeeper, but his real desire was to score goals.

"I am absolutely convinced that is the reason why he is such a clinical striker - he intuitively knows what the goalkeeper doesn't like. He shoots early when the goalkeeper's not set."

Bricknell: "I believe he was second top-scorer at Arsenal behind Benik Afobe, and then for some reason they decided at 11 years of age that they didn't want him any more."

The 'model student' with a Beckham Mohican

Kane attended Larkswood Primary Academy before moving to Chingford Foundation School, where he was inevitably the star of the football team. But, as a dedicated student, Kane impressed his teachers across the board.

Mark Leadon, Kane's PE teacher: "Aged 11, Harry was technically very gifted, with a great first touch, and a very clever player. He always knew where to go, right from an early stage.

"He was also a very good cricketer - he opened the bowling from year seven to 10 and batted at four or five. But he loved football. He was never a prima donna, and he would always put a shift in.

"What came through more than anything else was his determination to succeed. That work ethic was clear."

Luke Robinson, Kane's childhood friend and team-mate: "The only thing on his mind was football.

"We used to have a laugh, a couple of games of Fifa, but he was always driven. He'd always keep himself to himself.

"He loved David Beckham, he came in with the Mohican, everyone was laughing but he loved it. He loved football, 24/7, he lived and breathed football."

'Gold medallist? He wasn't even on the podium'

It was Tottenham Hotspur who offered Kane hope after his earlier disappointments, but the future England captain was by no means the pick of the bunch for his age group.

Kane's desire to learn and improve endeared him to the Tottenham academy staff and he signed scholarship terms with the club on his 16th birthday in July 2009.

Alex Inglethorpe, former Tottenham youth-team coach: "When I joined Spurs as under-18 coach, Harry was 13.

"I'd like to say he was the gold medallist in the group and we'd all spotted he was going to be the fantastic player, but I'd be lying. He probably wasn't even on the podium.

"If there was something that endeared him to you it was that he was very, very low maintenance. It became fairly evident when Harry became a scholar he was someone who could finish.

"He was wonderfully demanding to coach because he always wanted to stay out and do extra. That obsession to improve is undoubtedly his greatest strength.

"It was probably around 16 he started having an impact on the youth team. We trusted him to come off the bench and have an impact - anywhere from right wing, number 10, centre-forward, sometimes in midfield."

Kane went to League One Leyton Orient - making his professional debut in January 2011 at Rochdale, coming on for veteran striker Scott McGleish. Kane would score five times in nine starts.

McGleish: "Harry was not like other Premier League players, where you feel they're going to come in 'Billy Big Time'. He wanted the experience of learning what I call men's football.

"From the word go he was ready to fight for his place. In training, he was willing to just knuckle down and work hard.

"You could see in training and subsequently the matches he had ability and a desire to go further, but you're still looking like a young 17-year-old: very slight, still needing to physically develop, not the quickest but technically excellent."

After a few first-team games for Spurs, he went on loan in January 2012 to Championship strugglers Millwall. Kane's nine goals helped save Kenny Jackett's side from relegation.

Former Millwall defender Alan Dunne: "I've seen a lot of players come to the Den and freeze, because within five minutes they're being called names they've never heard before and they can't cope with that pressure.

"But it didn't faze him - he was a focused lad, he was confident in his ability."

Former Tottenham manager Tim Sherwood: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall, and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there.'

"I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him."

After making his Premier League debut for Tottenham in August 2012, Kane was sent on loan again. The 19-year-old only made three appearances in the top flight for Norwich because of injury, and then had a loan spell at Leicester where he and future England team-mate Jamie Vardy struggled for regular starts.

After four loan spells in three seasons, Kane spent the entire 2013-14 campaign with Tottenham. But it was not until April, after Andre Villas-Boas had been sacked and replaced by Sherwood, that a 20-year-old Kane was handed his first Premier League start for Spurs, scoring his first top-flight goal in the process against Sunderland and also netting in the following two games against West Brom and Fulham.

Sherwood: "It didn't feel a gamble at all to give Harry that start. It was almost overdue to be honest.

"Roberto Soldado was in front of him in the team, and nobody wanted Roberto to do well more than me - but every single day in training Harry was outperforming him. He didn't let me down.

"Harry wanted to get to the top, and nothing was going to stop him achieving that because of the ability, desire and mentality he possesses.

"I was the biggest believer Harry Kane ever had, because I used to think he was a mix between Teddy Sheringham and Alan Shearer."

Kane never looked back after scoring 21 top-flight goals the following season - and earning his first England call-up in March 2015.

He ended up as the club's all-time top scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances - and three Premier League Golden Boots, but no trophies

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, who tried to sign him, said in 2023: "What an exceptional player – the numbers and, more than the goals, the quality. Harry Kane remains one of the best strikers I have ever seen in my life."

Former Spurs team-mate Son Heung-min: "Leader, brother, legend.

"Since day one it has been a joy to play by your side. So many memories, amazing games and incredible goals together."

Then Tottenham boss Ange Postecoglou: "Harry was brilliant throughout. You want to work with the best players and he is a hell of a striker and I thought he could help me.

"He has left an indelible mark at this football club, will go down as one of the greats."

The only thing missing from Kane's career CV was trophies - and in 2023 he joined German side Bayern Munich, where he has continued to impress.

He has scored 152 goals in 154 games for the club, won the Bundesliga Golden Boot three times and won two German titles and a German Cup.

Former Bayern defender Lothaur Matthaus: "Kane has reinvented the centre-forward game, as Manuel Neuer did with goalkeepers.

"I don't see a better striker in the world right now. Not just because of his goals, but because of his versatility and the positions he plays.

"Kane also demonstrates qualities as a passer, dribbler, and tackler. He is simultaneously a goalscorer, playmaker, box-to-box player, and tackler."

Ex-England striker Alan Shearer, speaking this summer: " To me he looks fitter and stronger than before.

"He's come into this World Cup off the back of a brilliant campaign for Bayern Munich and looks very sharp and very confident - as you would do after scoring 61 goals in one season. Those numbers are just ridiculous."

BBC pundit Chris Sutton: "He has to be in that bracket when you talk about the world's best. Harry Kane has instincts that are simply uncoachable."

Some of these interviews were first published in 2016.

articles.title: El público croata muestra su cariño a Olmo: "Muchas gracias por todo, Dani"
articles.standfirst: Tras su generosa donación al pueblo croata y el cariño y respeto que muestra siempre por el país.
articles.summary: Tras su generosa donación al pueblo croata y el cariño y respeto que muestra siempre por el país.
articles.body: Dani es español, pero parte de su corazón siempre será croata. Aquí lo acogieron con 16 años y lo formaron como futbolista y persona, algo que él siempre ha agradecido. Y no sólo de palabra, también con hechos. Hace unos días conocimos que desde que abandonó el país dona el 2% de su salario bruto a Vukovar, una ciudad que sufrió de lleno las consecuencias de la guerra de los Balcanes. El pueblo croata ha querido aprovechar su visita a Split para agradecerle tal gesto y, cuando anunciaron su nombre en el once titular, protagonizaron una sonora ovación que se alargó durante medio minuto. Además, el speaker lanzó un mensaje en castellano: "Muchas gracias por todo, Dani". En la rueda de prensa previa ya recibió el aplauso de los periodistas locales cuando contestó una pregunta sobre el tema. "No sabía que esto había salido a la luz. Cuando me fui me sentía en deuda con Croacia y quería devolverle algo, así que hemos decido hacer esa donación a las familias de Vukovar y Slavonski Brod. Sentí que tenía que darle algo a Croacia por todo lo que me había dado y pensé que hacerlo a través de Common Goal sería la mejor manera", explicó.

articles.title: El relato de Cristiano de las horas que hicieron explotar todo
articles.standfirst: El delantero portugués ha realizado un comunicado tras el lío con Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: El delantero portugués ha realizado un comunicado tras el lío con Jorge Jesus
articles.body: El tema de Cristiano Ronaldo y la selección de Portugal sigue siendo un tópico mundial del que hablar. Ha saltado, aún más, con el comunicado de Cristiano Ronaldo sobre su decisión de abandonar la concentración del conjunto luso. Tras el 'banquillazo' ante Noruega, Cristiano narra lo que ocurrió justo después: Cuarenta y ocho horas después, tuvimos una conversación: yo, el entrenador y Simão Coutinho, ya que había estado siguiendo nuestras conversaciones en agosto. Fue un momento profundo y muy franco, sin filtros. El acuerdo era simple: el entrenador comenzaría la rueda de prensa con este tema, intentando zanjar el asunto diciendo la verdad. Diría que yo nunca pedí jugar ningún minuto, que fue el entrenador, y nadie más, quien propuso el plan para esta concentración, y que fue un error hacerme calentar solo para no jugar, y que si volvía a suceder, no lo haría. CR7 acusó de forma directa a Jorge Jesus de tomar una actitud que no era la que esperaba: A petición del entrenador, se celebró una videoconferencia entre él, Simão Coutinho y Tiago Craveiro, en la que se resumió lo que habíamos hablado. Se elaboró un breve documento, que yo mismo revisé y que, con mi conocimiento, se le entregó al entrenador, tal como él había solicitado. La conferencia transcurrió como se esperaba: su actitud no tenía nada que ver con nuestra reunión; percibí expresiones y agresividad que considero inmerecidas, una actitud de "yo quiero, yo puedo y yo mando" que jamás me había mostrado, ni siquiera remotamente, en privado, el día anterior. Cristiano tomó la decisión de dejar la concentración lusa tras lo ocurrido con el técnico luso: Decidí abandonar el campo de entrenamiento sin esperar otra promesa incumplida. Para mí, la verdad sigue siendo lo más importante en las relaciones interpersonales. Por mucho que duela, quiero que me digan la verdad. De hecho, en una conversación que tuve con el presidente de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol y el entrenador la mañana de esa rueda de prensa, que seguramente pueden confirmar, reafirmé que si no me querían allí, simplemente debían decírmelo. Solo necesitaban ser sinceros conmigo. Yo lo aceptaría y prometí que prepararíamos algo hermoso, como sueño que sucederá, y nadie se enfadaría. Lo recuerdo como si fuera ayer. Respondieron al unísono que no. Que mi lugar estaba en la Selección Nacional.

articles.title: Cristiano no renuncia a la Selección y asume las consecuencias: "Después de cumplir sanción, estaré disponible"
articles.standfirst: El jugador luso explica en una carta su marcha de la concentración y pide disculpas por su decisión, al mismo tiempo que notifica su intención de seguir siendo convocado por Portugal
articles.summary: El jugador portugués explica en una carta su marcha de la concentración y pide disculpas por su decisión, al mismo tiempo que se
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo ha expresado en una carta sus razones para abandonar la concentración de la Selección de Portugal tras lío con Jorge Jesus después del primer partido ante Noruega. En ella, entre otras muchas cosas, ha comunicado su intención de seguir jugando con el equipo nacional. "Si estoy en buena forma física, jugando para mi club y, con suerte, marcando goles, después de cumplir mi sanción, estaré disponible, como siempre lo he estado, para competir y ganar con nuestra Selección Nacional". El jugador reconoce su error de marcharse antes de tiempo de su estancia con su Selección y se disculpa con la gente que está con él. "Pido disculpas al pueblo portugués que nos apoyó intensamente, pido disculpas a los aficionados y a quienes, sin ser portugueses, viajaron hasta allí para verme y a quienes pude haber decepcionado" También mostró su arrepentimiento ante los jugadores, pero con un dardo hacia su seleccionador: "Les debo una disculpa a mis compañeros de la selección nacional por abandonar la concentración. A pesar de la absoluta falta de confianza en la palabra del entrenador no debí haberlo hecho. La responsabilidad es exclusivamente mía". No obstante, Cristiano Ronaldo asume la gravedad de los actos que representa una figura como la suya y acepta la decisión que se tome sobre él. "Las consecuencias de mis actos deben ser evaluadas y sancionadas por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol. Creo que el castigo no debe atenuarse. No soy un jugador cualquiera; soy el capitán del equipo, y eso es un factor agravante". "Ya me he disculpado, pero sé que los actos deben tener consecuencias". "Cualquiera en el fútbol, como yo, sabe que, independientemente de la posición individual, las reglas son las mismas para todos", sigue. Cristiano concluye la carta demostrando su compromiso con el equipo nacional, como cuando falleció su padre. "Cuando pienso en la selección nacional, en lo que realmente pienso es en competir. Eso es lo que pensé el día que recibí la noticia de la muerte de mi padre. Estaba en el campo de entrenamiento con nuestra selección nacional y decidí quedarme allí hasta que terminara el partido del día siguiente. Hice por el país lo que nunca haría por ningún club", finaliza. Respecto a los castigos que puede recibir la leyenda portuguesa, el Reglamento de la Federación portuguesa recoge que pueden incluir sanciones económicas y deportivas. una suspensión de entre uno y seis meses y multa económica. "Cualquier jugador que, habiendo sido convocado regularmente, abandone injustificadamente o no se presente a un entrenamiento, un partido o cualquier actividad de las selecciones nacionales o relacionada con la representación deportiva de la FPF o Portugal, será sancionado con una suspensión de uno a seis meses", se lee en el reglamento. Adicionalmente, si el jugador es profesional, con una multa de entre 5 y 10 UC [entre aproximadamente 500 y 1.000 euros, siendo 102 euros por unidad de cuenta]". Además, el párrafo segundo del artículo 160 del Reglamento de la FPF dice lo siguiente: "La ausencia o el abandono conllevan la suspensión preventiva automática del jugador en los términos establecidos en este reglamento", añade el texto.

articles.title: Missouri OL Johnnie Jones Hospitalized, Needs Heart Transplant After Undergoing Medical Testing
articles.summary: Missouri freshman offensive lineman Johnnie "DJ" Jones has been hospitalized in Florida after undergoing tests that revealed his need for a heart transplant, head football coach Eli Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday.
articles.body:
Missouri freshman offensive lineman Johnnie "DJ" Jones has been hospitalized in Florida after undergoing tests that revealed his need for a heart transplant, head football coach Eli Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday.

Drinkwitz said team doctors first discovered a health issue after Jones joined the team this summer.

According to Drinkwitz, Jones was under observation for two weeks with his team before he was diagnosed with a "much more significant issue" by the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida. He remains there now, Drinkwitz said.

"Last week, we found out that Johnny's now on a heart transplant list... It's tough right now," Drinkwitz said. "Our thoughts and prayers are with him and his family as they go through this."

Jones, 18, joined Mizzou out of Venice High School in Venice, Florida.

A 4-star prospect, Jones capped his high school career as a starting left tackle for a team that reached the championship game in its division.

After an earlier pledge to join UCLA, Jones headlined Mizzou's early signing day last December as 247Sports ' No. 11 offensive tackle in the incoming 2026 class.

Drinkwitz first mentioned sending prayers to Jones in his on-field postgame interview following Mizzou's Saturday win over visiting Florida.

The coach said Tuesday he knew "Johnnie was watching our game."

"It's just hard—18-year-old with everything in front of him, and you're just not prepared for that kind of news," Drinkwitz said Tuesday. "Our team wasn't prepared for that kind of news.

"But we're praying for him, and I know a lot of Mizzou fans will hopefully join in that prayer, because he does need help in a hurry. We're pulling for you, buddy."

Jones has not appeared in a game this season for the Tigers, who are next scheduled for a Saturday home game against Texas A&M.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal forward not retiring but says he wants to be punished for walking out
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo says he is not retiring from international football but deserves to be punished for walking out on Portugal after head coach Jorge Jesus "broke his word to me".
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he is not retiring from international football but deserves to be punished for walking out on Portugal after head coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word".

The 41-year-old captain left his country's Nations League camp after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.

Al-Nassr forward Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice.

In a lengthy statement, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United player said he should be held accountable for his actions.

"The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the punishment should not be reduced," Ronaldo said.

"I have already apologised, but I know that actions have consequences."

Ronaldo's statement comes after Portugal head coach Jesus said there was no rift with the captain, following claims the five-time Ballon d'Or winner had refused to train.

Jesus said on Sunday that the door was still open for Ronaldo to play for the country's national team.

Ronaldo said that, provided he was "physically fit, playing with my team, and hopefully scoring goals", he would like to continue to play international football.

"After my suspension period ends, I will be available, as I always have been, to compete and win with our national team," he added.

BBC Sport has approached the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) for comment.

Ronaldo's statement, which ran to nearly 2,000 words, struck a conciliatory tone in places.

But he was also critical of Portugal coach Jesus as he provided his version of the dispute which prompted him to walk out on the squad last week.

He said Jesus had agreed a plan under which the forward would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness.

However, on the day of the Norway game, the 72-year-old coach told him he would play for 30 minutes.

"Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn't called on," Ronaldo said.

"The manager had broken his word to me."

A later meeting with Jesus produced an agreement for the coach to clarify matters at his next news conference.

Ronaldo said an eight-point document was prepared saying he had never demanded playing time, had respected Jesus' decisions and that the coach asking "someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona" to warm up without bringing him on had been a mistake.

Portugal's record appearance holder said the agreed notes did not require Jesus to apologise to him but said the coach's public remarks did not reflect their private discussion.

"The conference was what is known: the attitude had nothing to do with our meeting," Ronaldo explained.

"I heard expressions and an aggressiveness I believe I did not deserve, a "High and mighty" attitude that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before."

Ronaldo said it was the "second time" Jesus had "broken his word to me" and he decided to leave the training camp "without waiting for any further broken promises".

Prior to his appointment as head coach, Ronaldo said he had described Jesus - who had previously managed him at Al Nassr - as the "right choice".

Ronaldo had considered retiring from international football after this summer's World Cup - at which Portugal exited at the last-16 stage - and said he had written a letter to fans containing the words he wanted to tell them when he announced it, but he was urged to reconsider by the FPF's president on the flight home from the United States.

Ronaldo's behaviour drew contrasting opinions in his homeland with Jesus getting some support in the media and among fans at odds with those loyal to legendary player.

Ronaldo said that, despite the "absolute breakdown of trust" in Jesus' word, he should not have left and the "responsibility is mine alone", as he said sorry to his fellow players and Portugal's supporters.

He added: "I owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp... I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but a broken word has, for me, a defining impact."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal star breaks silence over national team walkout in statement
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo delivers on his promise to explain why he walked out on the Portugal camp as he accuses head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises and apologises to his team-mates and the people of Portugal in a 1,996-word statement published to his 679m Instagram followers
articles.body:
The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, also accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises in a 1,996-word statement to his 679m Instagram followers.

Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."

See how Ronaldo issued his full statement below

Ronaldo left the national team squad in Copenhagen on the eve of a Nations League fixture against Denmark after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway on September 27.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner claims in his statement that Jesus had told him he would play 30 minutes against Norway on the day of the game only to go back on his word.

"Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn't called on," Ronaldo said. "The manager had broken his word to me."

Ronaldo and Jesus, who used to work together at Al Nassr, subsequently held a meeting, which was also attended by the sporting director of the Saudi Pro League club, Simao Coutinho.

According to Ronaldo's statement, Jesus agreed to clarify the situation and say that his captain never demanded minutes and that it was a mistake to let him warm up without bringing him on.

Ronaldo says an eight-point document was drawn up to summarise what had been discussed in a subsequent meeting between Jesus, Al Nassr sporting director Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, the player's strategic adviser.

However, Ronaldo felt the Portugal head coach's press conference bore no reflection to the conversation they had shared, which he claims ended in Jesus asking him for a hug.

"It was the second time he had broken his word to me," Ronaldo said. "I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises."

Jesus denied that any such agreement had been made with the player in a later press conference on Sunday when he left the door open for Ronaldo to return to the Portugal fold.

Ronaldo apologised to his team-mates and the Portuguese people over his departure from the squad and said he will accept whatever punishment is handed down to him by the Portuguese Football Federation.

The forward, who is his country's record appearance holder and goalscorer, also said he hopes his international career will not be limited to simply playing in a farewell game for Portugal.

Ronaldo added: "I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity. I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone.

"I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that. But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing.

"That is what I thought on the day I was given the news of my father's death. I was at a camp with our national team and I decided to stay there until the end of the match the following day. I did for the country what I would never do for any club."

Sky Sports News has approached the Portuguese Football Federation for comment.

articles.summary: Aston Villa might lure Endrick to the Premier League, Bournemouth fight to keep hold of Alex Scott, top clubs are keen on Rayan Cherki, plus more.
articles.body:
Aston Villa might lure Endrick to the Premier League, Bournemouth fight to keep hold of Alex Scott and top clubs are keen on Rayan Cherki.

Aston Villa are ready to strike a loan deal for Brazil forward Endrick after the 20-year-old failed to impress Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho. (Cadena SER - in Spanish) , external

Paris St-Germain and Liverpool are interested in signing Rayan Cherki from Manchester City should the 23-year-old France midfielder become available. (Teamtalk) , external

articles.summary: Bastien Vautier (19+8) comanda el convincente triunfo bilbaíno ante el IgokeTRI
articles.body: El Surne Bilbao se estrenó en la Liga de Campeones con una sólida victoria en la pista del Igokea bosnio (79-92) en un partido que el equipo vasco afrontó con las bajas por lesión de dos de sus jugadores clave, el pívot Tryggvi Hlinason y el alero Darrun Hilliard. El francés Bastien Vautier (19 puntos y 8 rebotes) lideró un triunfo coral de los de Jaume Ponsarnau en el que todos los once jugadores disponibles, apenas 48 horas después del partido con prórroga del domingo en A Coruña, se remangaron primero para abrir brecha y en el momento clave frenar el ímpetu del Igokea en el cuarto final. Sin Hlinason, que se quedó en Bilbao con varios puntos de sutura tras el fuerte golpe en la cabeza que sufrió el domingo, ni Hilliard, lastimado en un tobillo en el Coliseum aunque viajó y se sentó en el banquillo, el equipo vasco frenó rápidamente la buena salida local y marcó pronto distancias en el marcador (6-13, m.4). Ponsarnau estiró al máximo la rotación, dando entrada a los once jugadores en el primer cuarto, y obteniendo una buena respuesta tanto en el tiro exterior como en la pintura con Vautier y el debutante Hustak. Por parte balcánica, el escolta serbio Lazar Stefanovic sostuvo a un Igokea al que los bilbaínos, más eficaces que brillantes, castigaron con un pleno de acierto en triples en los primeros seis tiros y un Vautier casi imparable bajo el aro hasta alcanzar una renta máxima de +15 (26-41, m.15) que se mantuvo al descanso (35-50). El Surne estiró la ventaja hasta un máximo de +18 (35-53) nada más comenzar el tercer parcial mientras el Igokea elevaba la intensidad física y hacía la goma en el marcador hasta bajar por primera vez de la barrera de los diez de desventaja (64-72) con un parcial de 8-0 en el primer minuto del cuarto final. Ponsarnau paró el partido y el Surne se recompuso apoyado en Vautier y en un Somogyi algo atascado en el lanzamiento, pero clave con sus nueve asistencias y un triple que junto al de Normantas a un minuto de final sofocó el amago de rebelión local y sentenció el trabajado triunfo del equipo vasco. 79.- Igokea: (21+14+21+23): Penn (7), Kovacevic (5), Manojlovic (6), Armotrading (4), Stefanovic (17) -quinteto inicial- Lazic (13), Delalic (11), Pierre-Louis (7), Antunovic (6), Topolovic (-) y Milosavljevic (3). 92.- Surne Bilbao (28+22+22+20): Somogyi (5), Darling (7), Ansorregi (7), Petrasek (8), Vautier (19) -quinteto inicial- Normantas (10), Frey (9), Duscak (4), Krampelj (12), Font (5) y Hustak (6). Parciales: 21-28, 35-50 (descanso), 56-72 y 79-92 (final). Árbitros: Peter Praksch (Hungría), Andris Aunkrogers (Letonia) y Elvis Binders-Coders (Letonia). Eliminaron por cinco faltas a Stefanovic (m.39). Incidencias: partido de la primera jornada de la Liga de Campeones disputado en el SD Laktasi de la ciudad bosnia de Laktasi.

articles.title: Merino vale muchos cuartos
articles.standfirst: España se clasifica con un doblete de su jugador fetiche, clave para doblegar la agresividad de Croacia
articles.summary: España se clasifica con un doblete de su jugador fetiche, clave para doblegar la agresividad de Croacia
articles.body: En un fútbol de premios, fanfarrias y tonteos no cabe Mikel Merino, un futbolista que es una contraseña de la felicidad para España. Su entrada renombró un partido ante una Croacia agresiva hasta que le duró el oxígeno. El doblete de Merino lleva a España hasta los cuartos de final de la Liga de las Naciones. El mérito es doble porque Croacia no es Benin. El grupo de Modric planteó un partido para campeones. España sabe responder en todo tipo de climas. Cuando aguanta no pierde pie, como en Wembley, espera su momento y no perdona. Después de que Inglaterra le pisoteara el corazón, Croacia compareció en el césped con el escudo apretado. Es tierra de genios, de inventores de jugadas en muchos deportes y no consienten dos verbenas consecutivas. A los diez segundos Oyarzabal ya encontró un cocodrilo en el tobillo. España, con sus dos estrellas recién cosidas, era la mejor vitamina para un grupo herido. Sin balón, Croacia se disfrazó de Argentina con una intensidad extrema de la que nace en las tripas del vestuario entre toallas, isotónicos y charlas de Modric; con balón, era una tropa de ladrones de balón y velocistas que arrrugaba la pizarra española. En la izquierda, un clásico, Perisic, con mucha trinchera tomada, agriaba la noche a Pubill. España, que había presentado una alineación de final mundialista, se encontraba con un mapa de partido antipático. Sólo Lamine, vigilado por medio país, causaba inquietud cuando encaraba a Gvardiol. Era la única luz en un colectivo en el que dominaba la angustia. No es bueno dejar toda la colada a Lamine Yamal. El rival se amontona y es entonces cuando hay que buscar otros fuegos artificiales. Faltaba la lucidez de otros días en Baena, Olmo y Oyarzabal. La intimidación croata había hecho pupa. El gol de Perisic, tras buena parada de Unai a Matanovic, anunciaba tormentas. Desde Wembley, cuando Inglaterra se hizo un monstruo durante media hora, España no se atragantaba con tanta frecuencia. El mismo Matanovic, un gigante del Friburgo, y otra vez Perisic, acariciaron la sentencia. España seguía sin encontrar un agujero en la zaga croata. El partido del roce, el choque y la refriega lo perdían los campeones del mundo. Faltaba saber hasta dónde llegaría el oxígeno de los croatas, que hacían faltas claras y las protestaban como una orquesta sinfónica. La respuesta fue inmediata. Croacia, sin su zumo de ira, se quedó sin balón mientras España secuestraba el partido y montaba ataques de balonmano en las barbas del área rival. Cuando el asunto se pone así al adversario sólo le queda rezar lo que sepa. Además, De la Fuente había dado paso a un futbolista que no tiene precio, Mikel Merino, que es mucho más que un amuleto. El sustituto de Baena empezó a pisar ese terreno que dobla el cuello de cualquier zaga. Se sabe que está, pero no cuándo va a aparecer. Merino es un lujo. Bajo el mando y la inspiración de Pedri, España bordeaba el gol. Cada balón que llegaba a Lamine se convertía en una piraña para los croatas, fundidos tras su imponente primera parte. En una combinación de muchas piernas en el área el balón llegó a la zurda de Merino. Gol, empate y el campeón estaba en Split. En el nombre de las matemáticas y de los posibles enfados vía clubes, De la Fuente sentó a Lamine. Unai salvó con una pierna un gol hecho de Perisic, expulsado después. Era un momento para elegidos. Merino recibió un balón dentro del área, controló como un portento y se sacó un zurdazo. Ahora sí, se fue al banderín. Un jugador de bandera.

articles.body:
Harry Kane scored twice as England cruised to a comfortable 3-0 win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League at Wembley on Tuesday.

Here's how I rated the players - and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Marc Guehi : But for a couple of lapses, cruised through the game. Started all four of England's matches during the extended international break. 6

Harry Kane : Historic night for the England captain becoming the country's joint-highest appearance-maker alongside Peter Shilton with 125 caps. Goes without saying he scored... twice. 8

James Garner (on 63, Anderson): More international minutes in his legs. 6

articles.title: Unai Simón da la noche a uno de los mejores amigos en el fútbol de Terzic
articles.standfirst: El actual técnico del Athletic fue asistente de Bilic, uno de los que le animó a entrenar
articles.summary: El actual técnico del Athletic fue asistente de Bilic, uno de los que le animó a entrenar
articles.body: El Athletic recuperará para el entrenamiento del jueves a todos sus internacionales después de que la selección española haya cerrado este martes su participación en la ventana FIFA -tanto en absoluta como en sub21- y Padilla lo haga esta madrugada de miércoles con México. Y en la última jornada de esta ventana FIFA ha destacado Unai Simón, que con sus buenas paradas ha sostenido el empuje de Croacia y ha contribuido a conseguir el billete para los cuartos de final de la Nations League. Simón (29 años) ha sido baluarte de Luis de la Fuente en el duelo ante la Croacia que dirige Slaven Bilic, que pasa por ser uno de los mejores amigos en el fútbol de Edin Terzic, actual entrenador del Athletic. El actual técnico rojiblanco fue asistente de Bilic durante casi 200 partidos entre julio de 2013 y noviembre de 2017 cuando Bilic fue primer entrenador de Besiktas, primero, y después West Ham. En el momento que Terzic quiso volar como primer técnico Bilic fue uno de los entrenadores a los que consultó cómo veía esa posibilidad. La buena sintonía entre Terzic y Bilic es notoria y la pasada semana el entrenador del Athletic se trasladó a Sevilla para seguir en directo el encuentro que enfrentó en Sevilla a España con Croacia. El alemán viajó en compañía de Mikel González, director de fútbol del Athletic, y un retraso en el vuelo de vuelta hizo que Terzic llegara tarde al entrenamiento del Athletic al día siguiente en Lezama. Simón es el portero de confianza de Luis de la Fuente en la selección y referente en el Athletic, con el que tiene contrato hasta 2029 sin cláusula de rescisión. Han sido varios los equipos que se han interesado por el nominado a mejor portero del mundo, pero el de Murgia siempre ha asegurado que estará en el Athletic hasta que el club rojiblanco lo considere.

articles.title: Substitute Merino scores twice as Spain win in Croatia
articles.summary: Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino comes off the bench to score twice as world champions Spain fight back from a goal down to beat Croatia in the Nations League...
articles.body:
Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino came off the bench to score twice as world champions Spain fought back from a goal down to beat Croatia in the Nations League.

Coach Luis de la Fuente's Spain went into this game looking to record their 11th consecutive win, but they fell behind in the 17th minute when Ivan Perisic headed in.

Croatia had been thrashed 7-0 by England in their previous Nations League fixture but were given a standing ovation at half-time in this game following a much-improved display.

However, Spain were stronger after the break and drew level in the 61st minute when Dani Olmo got onto a poor clearance and picked out Merino, who made no mistake.

Lamine Yamal saw a goalbound shot blocked as Spain pushed for the winner, before Perisic was sent off for Croatia just moments after seeing a strong effort saved. The 37-year-old was shown a second yellow for a foul on Marc Cucurella.

That dismissal perhaps proved costly and Spain snatched the three points two minutes from time when Merino latched on to a fine ball from Arsenal team-mate Martin Zubimendi before sending a brilliant finish into the back of the net.

Spain are top of League A - Group 3, three points ahead of England who comfortably beat the Czech Republic 3-0 on Tuesday.

articles.title: Ronaldo apologizes for leaving Portugal camp, blames Jorge Jesus for broken promises
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has apologized for leaving Portugal camp midway through the international window, but also accused head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promi...
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has apologized for leaving Portugal camp midway through the international window, but also accused head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises in an extraordinary statement released on Tuesday, Oct. 6.

Ronaldo walked away from his national team amid a spat with Jesus, departing Copenhagen on Wednesday, Sept. 30, one day before a UEFA Nations League match against Denmark.

The 41-year-old started and played 65 minutes in a 1-0 win over Wales on Sept. 24, Portugal's first match of the window and the first match for Jesus, who took over from Roberto Martinez after the 2026 World Cup.

But the issue arose from Portugal's next match, a 2-1 win over Norway on Sept. 27. Ronaldo was an unused substitute in that game, and angrily walked down the tunnel at the final whistle instead of acknowledging Portugal's traveling fans with his teammates.

In Tuesday's statement that went more than 2,000 words , Ronaldo began by saying that he had endorsed the appointment of Jesus after the World Cup, having previously worked with the 72-year-old at Al Nassr.

According to Ronaldo, Jesus convinced him to continue his international career and presented a plan for the first post-World Cup window to manage his workload: He would play the first and last matches in Portugal, and skip the intervening games in Norway and Denmark.

Ronaldo said on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant coach told him to prepare to play 30 minutes. Though that wasn't part of the alleged plan, Ronaldo agreed. However, after warming up during the match in Oslo, Ronaldo was not put into the match. Angered, he rushed down the tunnel at the full-time whistle.

"The coach had broken his word to me," Ronaldo said in his statement.

"At the end of the game, I just wanted it all to end with a victory and to be alone. I didn't go to greet the fans. A mistake that is solely my responsibility and that shouldn't have happened. I apologize to the Portuguese people who supported us intensely there, I apologize to the fans, and I apologize to those who, without being Portuguese, may have traveled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed," the veteran forward added.

After the Norway match, Ronaldo met with Jesus and Al Nassr sporting director Simão Coutinho. At that meeting, Ronaldo said that he approved a list of talking points for Jesus to say at his next press conference.

Jesus was allegedly supposed to clarify that Ronaldo had never demanded to play against Norway, that he was "exemplary, loyal, and professional" and, among other talking points, the coach was allegedly going to utter the following line:

"I made a mistake by having someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona warm up and then not put him in the game. If it happened today, I would not do it."

But Jesus did not stick to the script during his press conference, which Ronaldo said was the last straw. He left camp that day.

"It was the second time he failed to keep his word," Ronaldo said of Jesus.

Cristiano Ronaldo ends World Cup career as Spain defeats Portugal

Ronaldo apologizes, ready to accept punishment

Ronaldo concluded by apologizing to his teammates and saying that he was prepared to accept any punishment that was headed his way.

Notably, he did not declare that he would never play for Portugal again, whether under Jesus or any other manager. In fact, Ronaldo said he would be available for selection after serving an expected suspension.

"I also owe an apology to my teammates for abandoning the training camp," he said. "Despite the complete breach of trust in the coach's word, as anyone who witnessed these conversations can attest, I shouldn't have done it. The responsibility is solely mine."

He added: "The consequences of my actions must be evaluated and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation.

"I believe the punishment should not be mitigated. I am not just any player; I am the team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor. I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences."

The 41-year-old has made 234 appearances for Portugal, and is the all-time leading scorer in men's international soccer history with 146 goals.

articles.title: Indiana Trolled by CFB Fans for Weak Non-Conference Schedule After Canceling 2027 UMass Game
articles.summary: Indiana football may be the defending national champions, but that hasn't stopped them from receiving criticism for their relatively weak schedule.
articles.body:
Indiana football may be the defending national champions, but that hasn't stopped them from receiving criticism for their relatively weak schedule.

The Hoosiers were under even more fire on Tuesday after cancelling their 2027 matchup with UMass and instead scheduling Jacksonville State.

Earlier this week, former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer said the Hoosiers' three wins over non-Power 4 teams shouldn't count.

"Indiana's 2-0 to me," Meyer said on The Triple Option podcast. "I don't watch the highlights. I don't care. I look at Ohio State's close loss to Texas as a much better performance than playing Howard. Why would you look at that? I don't think it should count."

After the announcement on Tuesday, some fans suspected that Indiana called off the game following UMass' 4-1 start to the season that includes a win over Rutgers.

To be fair to Indiana, plenty of college football fans and analysts criticized its schedule last year, and the Hoosiers went on to prove that they were the best team in the country.

With a relatively easy schedule again this year, Indiana will once again look to prove its doubters wrong.

articles.title: Georgia vs. Alabama Reportedly in Danger Due to 'Extreme Weather,' Latest Forecast for CFB Showdown
articles.summary: The biggest game of the Week 6 college football slate is No. 2 Georgia visiting No. 6 Alabama in Tuscaloosa, but a potential hurricane making landfall could force the game to get moved, per iconic ABC 33/40 chief meteorologist James Spann in remarks to Michael Casagrande of AL.com.
articles.body:
The biggest game of the Week 6 college football slate is No. 2 Georgia visiting No. 6 Alabama in Tuscaloosa, but a potential hurricane making landfall could force the game to get moved, per iconic ABC 33/40 chief meteorologist James Spann in remarks to Michael Casagrande of AL.com.

"We've got potential for a hurricane making landfall in Mobile Bay," Spann told AL.com. "The Alabama-Georgia game, a presidential visit, College GameDay. You got the big (Zach Bryan) concert at Auburn. This is the National Shrimp Festival at Gulf Shores this weekend, which is huge. I mean, you could not … it's gonna be a nightmare."

Spann added: "The idea of moving the game, it's on the table. I'm saying it's clearly on the table. It would be a nightmare for everybody involved. But if we do get a Category 1, Category 2 hurricane coming right up Mobile Bay Saturday morning, I don't know if you wouldn't be playing that game in Tuscaloosa that you've got the chance of winds gusting to 50 miles an hour, torrential rain and the chance of isolated tornadoes on top of everything else."

The latest Weather Channel forecast for Tuscaloosa on Saturday evening calls for a 90 percent chance of rain, noting a "potential for heavy rainfall" and "winds SE at 10 to 20 mph." The current call is for "rainfall around a quarter of an inch."

That wouldn't stop the game on its own, but there's a clear chance here that the forecast could get much worse, based on Spann's report.

We are still four days from game time, though, and Spann noted there isn't enough information at this time to make a call on the game.

"There's not enough confidence in a forecast to make any decision right now," Spann told Casagrande. "We'll have the data tomorrow. Hurricane Center will initiate advisories on it this afternoon. And (Wednesday) you've got the information you need to make a decision. So, we're probably about 24 hours away (at 1 p.m. Tuesday) if they decide to move the game and hopefully they won't."

The key, ultimately, is the storm's direction from the south.

"Aside from slowing down or changing directions wildly, Spann said the best case would be the storm moving east so the dry side would hit most of Alabama," Casagrande noted.

Spann said that if the storms arrives through West Alabama or Mississippi, then "it's gonna be rough. I mean, real rough."

Per Weather Channel , if winds reach at least 39 mph, then the storm will be called Tropical Storm Isaias.

"Tropical Depression Nine has formed in the western Gulf and is likely to become Hurricane Isaias before it brings heavy rain and gusty winds to the Gulf Coast from Louisiana to Florida," the Weather Channel noted.

"Isaias is expected to become the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season."

It's ultimately wait-and-see right now as far as Isaias' impact and path goes. As for the game, the SEC has an eye on the weather.

"Like we do every week at this time, we're keeping an eye on forecasts and staying in communication with schools with games that could be impacted by weather," a SEC spokesperson told John Talty of CBS Sports.

The two teams don't have a common bye week the rest of the season, so it's not clear when a makeup game would occur or how the SEC would reschedule the matchup. At this time, though, the game remains on for Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Messi: se va el más grande (con perdón...)
articles.standfirst: La opinión de Juan Castro sobre la despedida de Leo Messi
articles.summary: La opinión de Juan Castro sobre la despedida de Leo Messi
articles.body: Se va el más grande. Así lo creo, aunque le tenga mucho respeto (y devoción) a mi amado 'Diez' (Diego Maradona) y a los tres Mundiales ganados por Pelé. Nadie me hizo sentir el fútbol como 'El Diez'. Imposible que alguien le supere... y reconozco que mi vinculación personal con el Diego condiciona esta opinión. Pero, dicho eso, Leo, por números, me parece el más grande de la historia. Y el más grande se va hoy. Sus tres finales Mundiales; su campeonato del mundo; sus records individuales en Mundiales; sus registros en títulos colectivos; su trayectoria en el Barça; su longevidad de dos décadas en la élite; su, su, su... Cosecha tantos logros que es hasta redundante enumerar sus méritos. Es el más grande... y Argentina se queda huérfana de un líder absoluto (más allá de Scaloni). Por eso, alcanza aún más trascendencia el campeonato del mundo de España: contra el más grande; contra la que (era) la mejor Selección del planeta (ahora es La Roja); contra todo... se ganó, y con 'baile' en el juego. Por eso, nunca hay que dejar de festejarlo. Jamás. Pero, volviendo a Leo, siempre escribí que, tras estar en seis Mundiales y siete Copas Américas con el astro, admiro de él su genialidad pero, más aún, su resiliencia. Pocos cracks fueron tan criticados como él en su país, y Leo siguió y siguió luchando, con la cabeza alta y el orgullo intacto. Por eso, el éxito de sus últimos cinco años en la Albiceleste tiene aún más mérito. En fin, se nos va el Messi Albiceleste, pero queda el Messi jugador y el Messi empresario, con varios proyectos apasionantes en España. Se va el mejor. ¡Gracias por el fútbol, Leo!

articles.summary: Sulejmanovic (20+7+2), Birgander (14+6+5) y Ricky Rubio (6+5+7), destacados en la Penya
articles.body: El Asisa Joventut arrancó su andadura esta temporada en la Liga de Campeones de la FIBA con un triunfo por 86-75 ante el Bnei Herzliya israelí en un duelo dominado por el equipo badalonés desde el segundo cuarto. Los locales, que el fin de semana no jugaron su duelo ante el MoraBanc Andorra debido al temporal de lluvias en Cataluña, volvieron a disputar un encuentro oficial, en el que destacó Emir Sulejmanovic, con 20 puntos. El conjunto israelí comenzó mucho mejor el encuentro, con un parcial de inicio de 6-14 comandado por Amit Gershon, con ocho puntos prácticamente consecutivos que motivaron el primer tiempo muerto de Dani Miret. Como era de esperar, el Asisa Joventut reaccionó y lo hizo cuando entró a pista Nico Laprovittola, que se puso el equipo a sus espaldas para igualarlo todo en el luminoso (16-16, min. 8). En los últimos dos minutos del primer cuarto no hubo apenas canastas, tan sólo una de los verdinegros, que lo acabaron con un ajustado 18-16 que no gustó a su entrenador. El guión no cambió mucho en el inicio del segundo periodo, con una Penya fallona, y el Herzliya lo aprovechó para volver a ponerse por delante después de unos buenos minutos de DJ Burns (21-23, min. 12). Tras otro tiempo muerto de Miret, hubo reacción local y el Asisa Joventut logró una pequeña brecha tras una buena acción del joven Diego Niebla (35-30, min. 18). Una ventaja que fue a más con la entrada a pista de Simon Birgander, que fue pieza clave en el juego interior y los catalanes se fueron con un 42-33 al tiempo de descanso. En la reanudación, el Asisa Joventut mantuvo el buen nivel del tramo final de la primera mitad y Álex Reyes se quiso sumar a la fiesta anotadora desde la línea de tres para poner tierra de por medio en el Olímpic (47-36, min. 23). Pese a los múltiples intentos de los visitantes de rebajar la desventaja, los de Dani Miret siguieron sólidos y otro triple, esta vez de Kwan Cheatham, mantuvieron la ventaja (57-45, min. 28). Los últimos minutos de tercer cuarto se convirtieron en un intercambio de canastas que lógicamente benefició al equipo que iba por delante, el Joventut, que acabó el periodo con un 63-52 que dio tranquilidad, pero que no cerró aún el encuentro. Ya en el último periodo, Emir Sulejmanovic fue importante en el juego interior para que la Penya siguiera sumando y se acercara cada vez más hacia el triunfo (69-56, min. 32). Cuando parecía que los verdinegros podían sentenciar, en el Herzliya apareció Nathan Knight desde el perímetro para meter el miedo en el cuerpo a los locales en los últimos minutos de juego (76-67, min. 36). Los visitantes tuvieron opciones de rebajar más la desventaja, pero el Asisa Joventut quiso cerrar el choque lo antes posible, cosa que lograron, y finalmente los catalanes vencieron por 86-75 para ser líderes de grupo desde la primera jornada. 86 - Asisa Joventut (18+24+21+23): Rubio (6), Ellis (4), Reyes (6), Ndiaye (5), Birgander (14) -cinco inicial-; Laprovittola (11), Hakanson (6), Sulejmanovic (20), Torres (-), Nogués (-), Niebla (2) y Cheatham (12). 75 - Bnei Herzliya (16+17+19+23): Brewton (20), Carter (5), Bryant (13), Gershon (11), Burns (12) -cinco inicial-; Francis (1), Hannahs (5) y Knight (8). Árbitros: Yohan Rosso, Ioannis Agrafiotis y Tomasz Langowski. Eliminaron por cinco faltas personales al jugador local Sulejmanovic (min. 39). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase regular de la Liga de Campeones de baloncesto disputado en el Palau Municipal d'Esports de Badalona.

articles.title: England winners and losers: Who impressed and who is sweating over their Three Lions spot after four-game international break?
articles.summary: England won three games in their lengthy Nations League camp, losing the other game to Spain; Thomas Tuchel's side have breathed fresh life into their momentum after their disappointing World Cup exit, but some issues remain...
articles.body:
England's four-game Nations League camp started with a defeat to Spain but ended with two wins over Czech Republic and a 7-0 demolition of Croatia.

But after countless withdrawals and changes to the squad, who is feeling more confident about their England squad status - and who is starting to look over their shoulder?

Here are the winners and losers of the latest England squad...

It turns out that Anthony 'Barcelona' Gordon is a thing after all. For so long, England's left wing position was left open to debate. Nobody really claimed it as their own, even at the World Cup just gone.

Now the debate is over. That spot is Gordon's for as long as he stays fit and firing.

Three goals and one assist during this international break means the 25-year-old is at the peak of his powers. That form is even more surprising given he is yet to get off the mark for Barcelona this term.

It seems slightly odd to claim this international break a success for someone who has suffered a two-month injury during it. But Alex Scott is here to stay.

In the 7-0 win over Croatia, Scott showed he belonged at that level, playing the Declan Rice role to perfection.

His understanding with Elliot Anderson also shone through. That will be crucial for him going forward, given the pair were the midfield pivot for the most recent Euros-winning England U21 team.

It has worked for England at a major tournament before, it can work in the future. Scott's emergence has given Tuchel a real rotation option in that role.

Tuchel's first post-World Cup team selection had one major talking point. For the first time in nearly a decade, England played a big game without Jordan Pickford in goal.

Was the decision to start James Trafford in goal against Spain the first sign of a changing of the guard in the England goal? Never before has an England goalkeeper had this big an opening to usurp Pickford.

After Trafford started the Spain and the Czech Republic games, Pickford returned to Tuchel's line-up for the last two internationals. The No 1 shirt is not Trafford's, but the fact this role is now somewhat shared is a huge plus for the Leeds 'keeper.

Part of the Three Lions' recent spike in form at left wing has a lot to do with Lewis Hall's form down that flank. After so many tournaments of inverted options and waiting for Luke Shaw to be fit again, England have a natural option on that side again.

The Newcastle defender deserved the assist for Kane's second goal against Czech Republic at Wembley. England look balanced on that side again, and if Hall can stay fit then the head coach has one less thing to worry about.

So it turns out Trent Alexander-Arnold can play at right-back for England.

Two starts against the Czech Republic have got people talking about the much-maligned Real Madrid man in a more positive light again.

Alexander-Arnold looks back to his best, showing his creativity in Prague but the way he stretched Czech Republic at Wembley was also impressive.

He can play behind Bukayo Saka and impress. He can do the same with Morgan Rogers and also impress. Is this the camp where Alexander-Arnold's international career turned a corner?

This wasn't a standout camp from the England captain, but it's not gone unnoticed how Harry Kane just keeps on winning in an England shirt.

That's 91 goals in 125 England caps now. He has scored in nine out of his 14 matches for England in 2026.

But delivering in every game has become normal for him now. Just give him the Ballon d'Or.

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among the first players to pull out of this England squad. Their withdrawals came not even 24 hours after they played most of the 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Is there a way back for either of the Manchester United players?

Not only is their form at United under scrutiny, but others have stepped up in their absence. For Rashford, Gordon has now pulled clear of the United man in terms of the left-wing battle. And with Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze among Tuchel's favourites, is there still a spot in the squad for Rashford?

For Mainoo, the performance of Scott against Croatia risks putting the United midfielder further down Tuchel's pecking order.

He was already pretty low on that list after a minute-less World Cup, with the likes of James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White putting further pressure on both he and Rashford.

You wonder if either Rashford or Mainoo regret pulling out of this England picture so swiftly.

Chelsea's Cole Palmer was another player who pulled out of this England set-up early, with load management deemed to be the reason for his withdrawal.

But this international break has proven that Palmer is no closer to breaking the attacking midfield mould that Tuchel has in Jude Bellingham and Rogers.

Bellingham scored or created four out of the seven goals for England against Croatia. He remains untouchable in this team as a world beater. Rogers also scored in that game and is another Tuchel favourite.

After getting back to some form with Chelsea, this was a perfect window for Palmer to muscle his way back in. But he seems further back than ever in Tuchel's plans.

Reece James started out as England's first-choice right-back. When he was fit, he started, no questions. But has he ended up much further down the right-back pecking order now?

Alexander-Arnold's displays at right-back during this England camp have brought him back into the right-back equation. That spells trouble for James' starting hopes for England.

And after Jarell Quansah impressed against Croatia, England's right-back situation is becoming crowded. Could James be the one to make way from Alexander-Arnold's form?

Why Tuchel is both a winner and a loser from this camp

This was always going to be a sticky camp for the England head coach, who came into the Nations League campaign needing to earn trust and confidence back after those substitutions against Argentina.

Because of that, this was branded a 'lose-lose' for Tuchel. Any standout win and people will question where that performance was in the World Cup semi-final. Any defeat would have sparked more doubts about his credentials and potential at this level.

There are still concerns about Tuchel's England. His confession that England are still a "danger" to themselves while in possession of the ball echoed his controversial 'DNA' comments from the summer. The Three Lions still feel a long way off Spain's level where they are efficient in both boxes at the same time against the very best.

But the 7-0 win over Croatia - which caught everyone by surprise - has breathed fresh momentum into the Tuchel England era. That would have got the world of football talking.

There's also a bit more clarity in certain positions. England have two natural full-backs again, the left wing position is sorted. Players like Rice and Saka can be managed more with adequate replacements such as Lewis-Skelly, Scott and Rogers.

After clarity though, must come consistency. Tuchel has picked these players - they must stay there. Only that creates cohesion ahead of Euro 2028.

articles.title: England 3-0 Czech Republic: Harry Kane marks record-equalling 125th cap with two goals and an assist in Nations League victory
articles.summary: Report as England beat Czech Republic 3-0 in their final Nations League match of the lengthy international break; Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton's England appearance record and got two goals and an assist on his 125th cap; Vladimir Coufal scored a comical own goal at Wembley
articles.body:
The England captain's century and a quarter of caps is now level with Peter Shilton's all-time record that stood for 36 years - and it was a fitting display as he was involved in every single goal on the night.

Kane set up the first - his versatility to peel off to the right wing was rewarded as his cross was comically put into his own net by Czech defender Vladimir Coufal. Wembley almost unanimously laughed at the former West Ham man as the replays were shown on screen.

And Kane's moment came five minutes before half-time, as a sumptuous move involving Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers resulted in the latter crossing for his captain - who had all the time and space to finish.

It wouldn't be long until Kane sought to double his tally after the break. He struck the bar from distance but he eventually made it three when he headed Lewis Hall's delivery into the bottom corner at the far post.

Thomas Tuchel's England end the lengthy international break with three wins from four and 14 goals to show for it. Even though Spain beat Croatia 2-1 with a late comeback win to lead the group, England are all-but assured of a quarter-final spot anyway - needing one point from their last two games to qualify.

But this was Kane's night. No hat-trick for him as he was taken off with 10 minutes left - but he's now passed the 90-mark for international goals. He wants a century of goals to add to his appearance - and he's definitely going to get it.

5: CLOSE! Alexander-Arnold whips a free-kick over the Czech wall and it's tipped away by Hornicek.

27: OWN GOAL! Kane's cross is put into his own net comically by Coufal, who was under no pressure as he tried to clear.

30: OVER! Anderson misses a great chance to double England's lead but blazes over.

40: GOAL! Kane gets the goal on his big night as Anderson chips the ball over for Rogers down the right, who finds the England captain with acres of space to smash home.

54: OFF THE BAR! Kane is denied a second as his effort from the edge of the box clips the bar after great work from Myles Lewis-Skelly to start the free-flowing attack.

56: NEARLY! Rogers crosses for Bellingham whose deft flick is smartly denied by goalkeeper Hornicek.

57: GOAL! Kane heads in Hall's corner to double his tally on England's special night.

81: KANE OFF! The England captain is substituted for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, getting a standing ovation from Wembley. It won't be his last.

Tuchel's first post-World Cup camp assessed

This is Harry Kane's night, no doubt about it. But has Thomas Tuchel earned back a few more fans after this lengthy international camp?

Fourteen goals in four games against decent opposition. Croatia, Spain and Czech Republic are major tournament regulars.

There's a bit more clarity in certain England positions. Alexander-Arnold and Hall have had very good camps - when so many questioned whether they were right for this level. When was the last time England had two fixed, natural right-backs?

Jude Bellingham looks up for it and all the headlines are him are positive again. Anderson, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott have added depth to midfield.

And Kane keeps on doing the business. This set-up is built for him to thrive in. Are England back?

articles.title: Scotland 1-2 Slovenia: Sebastien Pocognoli still waiting for first Hampden Park victory
articles.summary: Match report as Scotland lose to Slovenia in the Nations League; Ryan Christie opened the scoring before the break; Aljosa Matko pulled the visitors level; Danijel Sturm put them ahead soon after Matko was denied a second; Scotland are third in Group B1 with two games to play
articles.body:
The Belgian was looking to end his first international window with a home victory to move the Scots up to second in Group B1.

Ryan Christie was brought into the starting XI as Pocognoli looked to add some creativity, and his decision paid off when the Bournemouth midfielder backheeled in the opener after Jack Hendry - back from suspension - headed off the post.

A win meant Scotland would sit second in Group B1 with two games left to play, but the visitors were determined to take that spot.

After Andy Robertson cleared Zan Vipotnik's effort, Aljosa Matko raced through and slotted in to pull level and the Scots looked rattled.

Danijel Sturm blazed an effort over the bar and Matko was denied a second by the offside flag before they did take the lead. The pair combined again, with Sturm guiding the ball home.

Scotland tried to find a way back into the game with soft penalty pleas quickly dismissed when both Findlay Curtis and Josh McPake were bundled over in the box.

It has been a tough start to the new Scotland era with just one win from four in this extended international break. They return to action next month for their final Nations League games against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

2: CHANCE! Ryan Christie finds John McGinn and he shoots first time from outside the area, but the shot is blocked.

13: OFF THE LINE! Danijel Sturm is played in down the left and cuts the ball to Adam Cerin but his effort is cleared by Jack Hendry.

31: GOAL SCOTLAND! Jack Hendry's header hits the post, Oli McBurnie misses the follow-up but Christie is there to backheel the ball into the net.

39: CHANCE! Zan Vipotnik is ready to tuck his effort into the bottom corner before Andy Robertson slides in to block.

52: CHANCE! Ben Gannon-Doak drives forward and lays it off for Christie to run onto but his shot is beaten away by Jan Oblak.

57: GOAL SLOVENIA! Aljosa Matko races through and slots his effort into the bottom left corner.

59: SLOVENIA SHOULD BE AHEAD! Sturm squanders a brilliant chance, blazing his effort over the bar.

69: NO GOAL! Matko pokes home what would have been his second goal, but the offside flag cuts his celebrations short.

72: GOAL SLOVENIA! Matko squares the ball to Sturm and he guides it home. Two goals in 14 minutes!

76: SCOTLAND WANT A PENALTY! Findlay Curtis has the ball in the area and is bundled to the ground but play is waved on.

78: ANOTHER PENALTY CLAIM! Josh McPake breaks into the area and, in a similar fashion to the first claim, he is bundled to the ground.

Scotland midfielder Ryan Christie speaking to BBC Scotland:

"A frustrating night. The first half wasn't particularly great but we came out a lot better.

"Then they get the goal and from there, we struggled. A frustrating way to end, especially given how we started the second half.

"Plenty to reflect on. It was nice to score but it feels a lot nicer when you win, that is the frustrating part.

"We didn't create enough tonight with the possession we had. All we can do now is reflect. We will be back in November.

"The previous game at home was a lot different. This is a lot more disappointing.

"This is a new group, a lot of youngsters, and they will gain experience. Hopefully, we keep building."

Monday November 16 - Switzerland (A), kick-off 7.45pm
